items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And Charlie was playing, and I had my guitar and I started chording and playing for him, and he turned around and he stopped playing

ctx.x: to play like Charlie Christian. I've been given credit for playing like Charlie or being influenced by Charlie, but I never -- I always admired his playing, he was a tremendous guitarist. But we thought differently, and I would go to hear Charlie every night in Minton's. That's when Dizzy was there, and Joe Guy and Monk. Let's see, the bass player was Nick Finton, and the saxophone player's name was Scotty.

And every night I would go there because Charlie would come by and play, and I admired his play. But I never wanted to play like him, because I heard different things, you know. His was a very exciting style and everybody just loved him, including me. And all the guitarists just jumped on his style. But I had to be me, and I guess I'm stubborn, you know. But I'm still getting a little ahead of my story because I want to tell you when I first met Charlie I had been on the road with Fletcher Henderson, and I'll get…
But it was a mutual admiration thing. But
